rules.statement: Code that only returns the public half of a stored asymmetric key must read stored public material and must not unprotect the private key or load master keys.
rules.why: Unprotecting a private key just to emit its public half loads the owner's master keys, may call the key management service, and keeps private key material in memory for what is a read of public data.
rules.check: Look for public-key or JWKS read paths that take an ISecretProtector, call unprotect/decrypt, or deserialize the private key to export its public key.

rules.statement: When storing the public half of a generated asymmetric key, store it as base64url SubjectPublicKeyInfo (SPKI) DER, not as a JWK or PEM.
rules.why: A JWK carries kid, use and alg, which can change after the key is stored, and PEM adds a second format; SPKI is what the key descriptors already deserialize.
rules.check: Look for stored public-key fields filled with JWK JSON or PEM text instead of base64url SPKI DER.

rules.statement: Store a separate public key only for private asymmetric keys; leave it null for symmetric secrets and for secrets whose stored value is already public (SPKI or X.509).
rules.why: For public-only secrets the stored value already is the public material, so a copy duplicates it, and storing the SPKI of an X.509 secret drops its certificate.
rules.check: Look for code that fills a separate public-key field for symmetric, SPKI or X.509 secrets, or that reads the public half of a public-only secret from that field instead of from its own value.

rules.statement: When a new field is added to a persisted record, every update handler that rebuilds that record must copy the new field over.
rules.why: Update handlers that rebuild the persisted record would otherwise silently drop the new stored value.
rules.check: In a diff that adds a property to a persisted entity, check that each update path that builds a new instance of that entity sets the new property.

rules.statement: When adding a member that implementers of an extensibility type must supply, declare it `required` so that every implementation, third-party ones included, has to set it on purpose.
rules.why: A `required` member makes every descriptor, third-party ones included, decide on a value instead of silently getting a default.
rules.check: Look for new members on records or result types that extension points fill in, where the member is optional or defaulted even though each implementation has to choose a value for it.
